body:
I think we need more updates, mostly to the non-normative introductory text. E.g. https://whatpr.org/html/7617/origin.html#origin-keyed-agent-clusters says

> A [Document](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/dom.html#document) delivered over a [secure context](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/webappapis.html#secure-context) can request that it be placed in an [origin](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/origin.html#concept-origin)-[keyed](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/webappapis.html#agent-cluster-key) agent cluster, by using the `Origin-Agent-Cluster` HTTP response header.

but it should probably say something like "By default, a Document is in an origin-keyed agent cluster. The Origin-Agent-Cluster header can be used to opt out of this behavior and become site-keyed."

Similarly, with the paragraph starting "The consequences of using this header are that the resulting [Document](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/dom.html#document)'s [agent cluster key](https://whatpr.org/html/7617/webappapis.html#agent-cluster-key) is its [origin](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin)..."

That's a good point. We also want to move/adjust this `document.domain` warning to instead cover this feature:

> Avoid using the [document.domain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-domain) setter. It undermines the security protections provided by the same-origin policy. This is especially acute when using shared hosting; for example, if an untrusted third party is able to host an HTTP server at the same IP address but on a different port, then the same-origin protection that normally protects two different sites on the same host will fail, as the ports are ignored when comparing origins after the [document.domain](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-domain) setter has been used.
> 
> Because of these security pitfalls, this feature is in the process of being removed from the web platform. (This is a long process that takes many years.)
>
> Instead, use [postMessage()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-window-postmessage) or [MessageChannel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#messagechannel) objects to communicate across origins in a safe manner.

Minor adjustments in "Integration with the JavaScript agent formalism" might be welcome as well, although I think the existing text could work.

Heya, it's been a while.

This change was launched on Chrome somewhere late '2023 and has been enabled ever since. I've rebased this spec PR to the current head.

An easy way to check is e.g. to go to https://www.example.org/ (which does not set any headers) and execute `document.domain = "example.org";` in the dev console. On any current Chromium-based browser this should no-op (with an error message).

I have not heard any user complaints in the recent months. Early user complaints focused on a particular, no longer sold but still maintained enterprise product. The vendor had provided a timely update but this required manual actions to update for each customer that was still using it, which apparently took a while. (Said vendor's newer products didn't have issues.)

I think now would be a good time to land this change.
Since this is a normative change, it would be good if it followed https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/main/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Based on a quick scan we need browser bugs and an MDN issue.

I am working with Daniel on finishing this up. I've updated the OP with the modern pull request template.

The biggest blocker is updating all the WPTs for the new default. Daniel is working on doing so. Once that is done, I'll link to the update, and take care of filing bugs and MDN issues.
All boxes in the OP are filled out, although Daniel's work on updating the tests is currently in "draft" status. (But they are all passing.) I'll merge this once those are slightly more far along.

I'm curious what the current status of this change is in Chromium, including what kind of opt-outs are still available such as reverse origin trials. Especially if there are still enterprise opt-outs as the linked bug suggests I'm not sure this is ready for standardization.

> I'm curious what the current status of this change is in Chromium, including what kind of opt-outs are still available such as reverse origin trials. Especially if there are still enterprise opt-outs as the linked bug suggests I'm not sure this is ready for standardization.

* This has been default-enabled since M115 (June 2023).

* The flag (which allows users to opt-out via UI or command-line) has been expired since M130 (Oct 2024).

* This feature never had an origin trial (reverse or otherwise), since if you can set headers on your site you can just set the `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0` header to solve the issue for good. An additional, time-limited header would have provided no benefit. (This feature only changes the default behaviour when no header is set, or the header value is invalid. Sites can still control the origin-agent clustering via the header.)

* There is an "enterprise policy" ([policies for enterprise-managed Chrome instances](https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/)) to opt-out. I don't think enterprise policies are usually expired at all, and I'm not aware of any plan to expire this policy. I'm surprised this would be a standards consideration.

* There were numerous requests to delay / opt-out around the time this was enabled. I don't recall any complaints when the flag expired. My conclusion is that by then the community had moved on.

* The support code for this is still in, since I hit a snag when wanting to remove the code. My bad. I should remove it...

Thanks! Good to know it's more or less complete.

The existence of an enterprise policy suggests that rolling this out might not be straightforward without an equivalent policy and getting adoption of it in the same policy. There was an equivalent concern with mutation events. With those we waited until the reverse origin trial expired. But maybe we try it out and see how it goes.

What I think remains here:

1. We need a complete PR for WPT or some guarantee the Chromium change is complete and will land within a 24h window of the specification change landing.
2. This need to be rebased so we get a completed CI build.

I discovered this has more issues as this is all conditional upon secure contexts so `document.domain` remains working in a number of places.
AI review ``` Summary The algorithm change is correct and matches Chromium: it keeps the step that sets requestsOAC to false for non-secure contexts (source:105338), so http stays site-keyed. But five prose changes drop that condition, and a note the PR didn't touch is now inverted. Roughly 2 blockers, 6 suggestions, 1 nit. Blockers - source:87821–87825 — The originAgentCluster note is now inverted. It says the getter "can return false, even if the header is set, if the header was omitted on a previously-loaded same-origin page … it can return true even when the header is not set". With the new default, a same-origin page that omitted the header was origin-keyed, so later pages read true. — Change to "can return true, even if ?0 is set, if the header was omitted on a previously-loaded same-origin page in the same browsing context group. Similarly, it can return false even when the header is not set." - The default is stated without its secure-context condition in five places. Non-secure contexts stay site-keyed and document.domain keeps working there, per the PR's own algorithm and per Chromium (DetermineOriginAgentClusterIsolation, and its browser test OriginAgentClusterInsecureEnabledBrowserTest.DocumentDomain_Default). - source:87581–87583 — "It is no longer available by default, because by default documents are placed in an origin-keyed agent cluster" → "It is no longer available by default in secure contexts, because documents in secure contexts are placed in an origin-keyed agent cluster by default". - source:87790–87793 — "By default, a Document is placed in an origin-keyed agent cluster." This also drops the old "delivered over a secure context". → "By default, a Document in a secure context is placed in an origin-keyed agent cluster, and other Documents in a site-keyed one. A Document in a secure context can use the `Origin-Agent-Cluster` HTTP response header to request a site-keyed agent cluster instead." - source:87808–87809 — "while in the default case it will do nothing" → "while by default it will do nothing in a secure context". - source:106900–106901 — "This is the default case." → "This is the default in secure contexts." - source:107000–107002 — "By default these will be origin-keyed agent clusters…". "These" also has no antecedent, since a key isn't an agent cluster. → "Without web developer action to achieve site-keyed agent clusters, it will be a tuple origin in a secure context and a site otherwise." Suggestions - source:87791–87792 — The rewrite dropped the opening backtick: The Origin-Agent-Cluster` HTTP, so the page renders a lone backtick. — Restore `…`. - source:87836–87838 — The cross-origin isolation note lost its

, and the deleted text leaves no statement about the header there. Under the new default, ?0 has no effect for cross-origin-isolated documents. — Close the

and add "For them, the `Origin-Agent-Cluster` header has no effect." - Chromium mismatch for https iframes under an http page: - The spec decides secure context from the top-level creation URL, so such an iframe stays site-keyed under this PR. - Chromium's gate (IsValidOriginForOriginAgentClusterOptIn) only checks the document's own origin, so its code origin-keys such an iframe by default. I haven't run Chromium. - WebKit honors ?1 there today, which is the bug I confirmed earlier. - The spec is the consistent choice, since it matches isSecureContext. This needs WPT coverage and a Chromium bug, not a spec change. - source:87809–87810 — "it will be possible to send WebAssembly.Module objects to cross-origin Documents (if they are same site)" is correct per the Wasm Web API. But Chromium rejects all cross-origin modules (DispatchMessageEventWithOriginCheck, WebAssembly/spec#1303), so even with ?0 it won't hold there. No change needed, but it cuts against the "match Chromium" rationale. - Tests: the PR body points at Chromium CL 4813806, but no WPT PR exists for it; the only related export is #32057 from 2021, which is https-only. - Nothing tests the http default (no header: document.domain works and originAgentCluster is false). insecure-http.sub.html only covers ?1 over http. - Also missing: the https-iframe-under-http case, and updates to tests that assume the old default. - This fits your 2026-09-27 comment asking for a complete WPT PR. - Commit message: add that documents in non-secure contexts stay site-keyed, so document.domain keeps working there. Nits - source:87811–87813 — "this can prevent user agents from allocating … in an efficient way" → "… from efficiently allocating …". Overall One more round, mostly on the prose: scope the default to secure contexts in five places and fix the inverted note. The WPT work is the real prerequisite. The PR still applies cleanly to current main (offsets only), so the rebase you asked for is trivial. I haven't posted anything to GitHub; I can draft a comment from this if you want. ```
